fix.summary: Two Plan-readiness blockers remain. First, freeze the capability contract rather than leaving aliases and transport/default semantics open: enumerate the existing child tool names, define how every allowed `bash` value is an exact complete command string, enumerate the package-owned prerequisite operations, select the structured task-digest-bound ceiling source, and state that absence or mismatch cannot default to a wider grant. Second, reconcile target chronology and ownership: exact base/material bytes must be resolved from an immutable runtime-pinned target before acceptance, but the Plan currently says the runner first prepares that snapshot only after acceptance while rejected proposals perform no snapshot operation. Specify one feasible seam—for example, dispatch-owned preflight pin/read prerequisites followed by runner-owned post-acceptance mirror/workspace execution—without giving the runner target-resolution or lifecycle authority.

details.note: Blockers 1, 3, and the main ownership correction are otherwise fixed: there is no broad `--ak-review-input` or caller-supplied target/material content; no-spec uses the same dispatch owner to run exactly one complete Standards child with no Spec construction or fake sibling batch; `reviewer-dispatch` owns proposal validation, compilation, capability intersection, and transitions; the runner is intended as an opaque executor; the ledger is an append-only evidence projection; and the Standards baseline is extracted only from the supplied canonical Skill snapshot. All six changes include Behavior/Owner/Red/Green/Scope, obsolete arbitrary-prompt/persisted-message/fake-Spec paths and fixtures are replaced rather than layered, and the proposed module boundary is otherwise bounded and deep. The unresolved capability ceiling and contradictory target-preflight chronology are construction blockers because they leave executable authority/default behavior and the only feasible owner sequence undecided.
